alerts.title: Untreated hypothyroidism likely driving weight gain
alerts.message: Patient has TSH 12.4 mIU/L with low Free T4, dry skin, periorbital puffiness, delayed ankle reflexes, constipation, and cold intolerance — all classic features of inadequately treated hypothyroidism. She admits often forgetting her levothyroxine. The 9 kg weight gain over one year is being attributed to DTG, but uncontrolled hypothyroidism is a strong alternative explanation. The clinician plans to switch DTG without first addressing levothyroxine adherence and dose optimisation. Switching DTG in a virologically suppressed patient (VL <50) without correcting the thyroid dysfunction may not resolve the weight gain and risks losing a well-tolerated, high-barrier regimen.

evidence.recommended_action: Optimise levothyroxine adherence and up-titrate dose to normalise TSH before attributing weight gain to DTG. Reassess symptoms and weight after thyroid correction before switching ART.

alerts.title: DTG hyperglycemia risk: multiple risk factors present
alerts.message: Guidelines require screening for hyperglycemia risk before DTG use; risk factors include age ≥40, BMI ≥25, and history of hypertension. This patient is 45, BMI 33, and on TLD since January 2023. Guidelines state that clients with 2 or more risk factors and high baseline glucose should not be on DTG. Her fasting glucose is 5.6 mmol/L (below the >6.95 threshold). However, guidelines recommend glucose monitoring every 3 months for the first year for those with risk factors. No repeat glucose has been checked since starting DTG over 3 years ago, representing a monitoring gap.

evidence.recommended_action: Assess hyperglycemia risk factors formally. If continuing DTG, monitor fasting glucose every 3 months. If switching, use EFV400 or ATV/r per guidelines for hyperglycemia risk.

alerts.title: Dyslipidemia — Grade 2 cholesterol and LDL
alerts.message: Guideline toxicity grading classifies fasting total cholesterol 6.4 mmol/L as Grade 2 (moderate, 6.19–7.77) and LDL 4.2 mmol/L as Grade 2 (4.12–4.90). Triglycerides 2.3 mmol/L fall in Grade 1. TDF can contribute to dyslipidemia, though DTG is generally lipid-neutral. Uncontrolled hypothyroidism is also a well-recognised cause of elevated cholesterol and may be a major contributor here. The clinician's plan does not address the dyslipidemia or its relationship to thyroid status.

evidence.recommended_action: Reassess lipid panel after thyroid function is corrected. If dyslipidemia persists, consider ART substitution or lipid-lowering therapy per guideline side-effect management tables.

alerts.title: Overdue TDF renal monitoring — creatinine not checked in 6 months
alerts.message: Guidelines require serum creatinine and eGFR every 12 months for patients on TDF. The last creatinine was 72 umol/L on 2025-08-12, 196 days before this visit. While this is within the 12-month interval, no renal monitoring is included in today's plan. Given the patient's weight gain, new metabolic abnormalities, and potential switch decision, a current renal function assessment would inform safe continuation of TDF or selection of an alternative backbone.

evidence.recommended_action: Check serum creatinine and eGFR at this visit to confirm TDF renal safety and guide regimen decisions if switching from DTG.

Hyperglycemia among previously non-diabetic adults and worsening of hyperglycemia among diabetics has been reported among clients on DTG. Although the hyperglycemia associated with DTG has been reported among clients newly initiated on ART as well as among those already on ART and transitioned to DTG-based regimens, the hyperglycemia appears to occur more commonly among the latter group. Adults being initiated on DTG should be screened for risk factors for hyperglycemia: * Age ≥ 40 years * BMI≥ 24 kg/m2 * History of hypertension * Known diabetics should not be initiated or transitioned to DTG. Give an EFV400 or an ATV/r-based regimen. * Clients with 2 or more risk factors for hyperglycemia and a high baseline RBS or FBS should not be initiated/transitioned to DTG. Give an EFV400 or ATZ/r-based regimen.
